newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: FORECAST - Portucel H1 profit seen higher.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST - Portucel H1 profit seen higher.

text.p: Portugal's bleached pulp concern Portucel Industrial is expected to announce on Friday that improved market conditions returned it to profit in the first half after its 1996 losses.
Of five analysts contacted by Reuters, three said Portucel would post a first-half net profit of between 600 and 800 million escudos and one thought the figure could be as high as 1.0 billion.

"Portucel will have made a first-half (net profit) of between 500 million escudos and 1.0 billion. This reflects the improvement in prices and volume of turnover in pulp during the second quarter," said one analyst at a Portuguese bank who declined to be named.
In 1996 Portucel posted a first-half consolidated loss of 2.9 billion escudos and a full-year loss of 1.4 billion.
"Since Portucel's results look positive for the first half, I think we can safely say that it will substantially improve its full-year profit," said another analyst.
"Given the recovery in the (pulp) market, I would expect first-half profit of between 700 and 800 million escudos," he added.
Portucel originally planned to announce its results on July 31 but later brought forward the announcement to tomorrow after 1530 GMT.

"Portucel will have made anything between a loss of 500 million and breakeven in the first half but the fact that they're now rushing to announce their result early suggests it may be positive," said a third, more cautious, analyst.
All five analysts agreed that higher pulp prices and reduced stocks would continue to boost Portucel's results this year and next.
"The trend changed as soon as the first price rise was announced and accepted by the market. This has been accompanied by a fall in pulp stocks," said the first analyst.
"Stocks will continue to fall, although there will be a slight seasonal rise during the summer. This will mean that prices will continue to rise until the end of the year and into 1998," he said.
Portucel raised its prices 40 Ecus per tonne to 490 from July 1, continuing the upward trend that started in April.
The first analyst said that Portucel could post 1997 profits of 4.5 billion while another thought the figure would be closer to 2.3 billion.
Salomon Brothers updated its profit forecast for Portucel in May, estimating it would finish the year with profit of 2.0 billion, rising sharply to 11 billion in 1998.
Portucel closed up 18 escudos today at 1,483 on volume of 641,584.
